items.title: ROAD CLOSED: Traffic lights out following crash in Mississauga
items.summary: Police say a set of traffic lights at a busy intersection aren’t working following a crash in Mississauga. m. at the intersection of Dixie Road and Dundas Street East in Mississauga, Peel Regional Police say. One of the drivers suffered minor injuries in the crash, police say. No additional details about the victim have been disclosed. Traffic lights at the intersection are temporarily offline, and police have closed the eastbound lanes of Dundas Street to all traffic east of Dixie Road. Police say the crash could cause delays for the next two to three hours. Drivers are being urged to avoid the area and find other routes if possible. TRAFFIC ALERT: – Dixie Rd and Dundas St E #Mississauga – Two vehicle collision. – Traffic lights at the intersection temporarily not working. – All E/B lanes closed on Dundas St east of Dixie Rd – Minor injuries to the driver. – Avoid the area. items.title: Activists Win Pause on Data Centres in Mississauga, but Questions Remain About Provincial Regulation
items.summary: Mississauga "one of the first big cities to address this matter and push back against this data rush” Activists in Mississauga scored a victory in the fight against unregulated data centres last week after city council voted unanimously to pause new large digital infrastructure projects for the next year. But despite their win, advocates are saying the job is far from over. On September 16, Mississauga city council voted to enact an interim control by-law (ICBL) to effectively freeze any new data centre project in the city with a peak-power demand above 10 megawatts for up to a year, which is enough energy to power 10,000 homes. ” Martin Reid, the councillor for Ward 9, where the data centre would be located, told PressProgress that he was really happy to see the ICBL get approved. “Putting development before planning is never a good idea,” said Reid. ” The Toronto suburb was set to host a new 220,000+ square foot, 40 megawatt data centre in its north end. A development application to create the two storey data centre was received by the city at the end of 2025.

items.title: Peel Police Investigate Possible Arson After Second Fire Hits Same Mississauga Building in a Day
items.summary: According to INsauga, Peel police are investigating Monday's fire at a seven-storey apartment building at 920 Inverhouse Drive in south Mississauga as suspicious, after learning it broke out less than a day after a separate blaze on the same floor of the building. Peel police Acting Sgt. Amanda Steenson said in an email that officers are treating the fire as suspicious. Firefighters were called to the scene early Monday morning and brought 11 fire apparatus, three command vehicles and roughly 43 firefighters to battle the blaze. Crews rescued about 16 people from balconies on the third and fourth floors using ladders and aerial fire trucks, according to fire officials. The building's fire sent 18 people to hospital in total. Peel police's 11 Division Criminal Investigation Bureau is now looking into both fires and is asking anyone with relevant information to contact investigators.

items.title: Families of Victims Set to Address Court as Mississauga Man Faces Sentencing in Assisted-Suicide Case
items.summary: According to INsauga, friends and relatives of people who died after using items purchased online from Kenneth Law are expected to address the court this week as the Mississauga man faces a sentencing hearing. Law pleaded guilty in late May to 14 counts of aiding suicide in the deaths of 14 people across Ontario, including some victims who were minors. That plea came weeks before Law was set to stand trial on those charges along with 14 counts of first-degree murder connected to the same victims, and prosecutors have said they intend to withdraw the murder charges once he is sentenced. A conviction for aiding suicide can carry up to 14 years in prison, and lawyers for the Crown and defence are expected to argue for what each side considers an appropriate sentence. The hearing is also meant to give loved ones of those who died a chance to describe in court how Law's actions affected them. According to an agreed statement of facts read in court, Law ran several websites that sold sodium nitrite and other products that can be used for self-harm, and shipped roughly 1,200 packages to recipients in more than 40 countries, including close to 160 packages sent within Canada.

items.title: Failed Food Storage and Pest Control Checks Shut Down a Britannia Road Pizza Shop
items.summary: According to INsauga, Peel Public Health inspectors temporarily closed Karachi Pizza, a Karachi-style gourmet pan pizza restaurant at 812 Britannia Road West, after an inspection on Tuesday, September 22 turned up significant health violations. The inspection report found the restaurant failed to properly store food in a way that prevents contamination, and did not take adequate steps to keep pests out, creating health risks for customers. Inspectors also found insufficient lighting and non-food contact surfaces that were not kept clean and sanitary, according to the report. Peel Public Health issues a green card for a passed inspection, a yellow card for a conditional pass involving minor infractions, and a red card when significant health risks are found, forcing the establishment to close until it passes a follow-up inspection. Karachi Pizza received a red card and must pass that follow-up inspection before it can reopen. Mississauga.com reports the same round of inspections also produced conditional passes for two other local restaurants, Chai Churi and Toronto Sweets & Snacks Factory.

items.title: Port Credit's Crooked Cue Pub Traces Back to a 1937 Movie House Now Headed for Heritage Status
items.summary: According to INsauga, a report to the City of Mississauga's Heritage Advisory Committee recommends heritage designation for the building at 75 Lakeshore Road East in Port Credit, now home to The Crooked Cue pub and pool hall but originally built as the Vogue Theatre. Farrow and Sons constructed the theatre on a then-vacant lot in 1937, and it seated 500 people during an era when movie-going was booming, the report says. The Port Credit Businessmen's Association had pushed for a movie house in the village to compete with nightlife across the border in New Toronto, now part of Etobicoke, and Oakville already had its own theatre by that point, according to the report. Before the Vogue was built, residents watched silent films at Clarke Hall, but that venue struggled once talking pictures arrived in the late 1920s. Construction of the new theatre took just two months, the report notes, and the finished brick building featured a cream and white street front with an Art Deco marquee. Its upper level was rented out to a salon and a dentist's office, according to the report.

items.title: Over 3,200 Tickets Issued So Far as Mississauga's Waterfront Parking Crackdown Nears Its End
items.summary: According to INsauga, the City of Mississauga says the number of parking tickets issued along its waterfront during late spring and summer has dropped by hundreds since the city raised seasonal fines to $100 back in 2021. For the past five years, the city has more than doubled fines for illegal parking and stopping within what it calls the Lakefront Increased Penalty Zone, an area south of Lakeshore Road, running each year between May 1 and the end of September. City officials say the annual initiative is meant to discourage illegal parking and reduce traffic congestion during the busiest months on and near the waterfront, which they say draws thousands of residents and visitors. As of September 16, the city had issued 3,241 penalty notices during this year's Lakefront Increased Penalty Zone campaign, according to INsauga. That 2026 initiative is set to wrap up the following Wednesday. The city says the higher fines have contributed to fewer violations in the zone compared with years before the increase.

items.title: Dozens of Overnight Vehicle Break-Ins Across Mississauga End With One Arrest and a Continued Search
items.summary: According to Peel Regional Police, a string of vehicle break-ins that hit neighbourhoods across Mississauga between September 3 and September 6 has led to one arrest, with officers still searching for a second suspect. Police say the overnight break-ins involved 71 vehicles that were entered unlawfully, though no vehicles were taken and none were occupied at the time. Investigators allege valuables were stolen from inside the vehicles during the spree. A 34-year-old man with no fixed address has been charged with 46 counts of attempting to commit an indictable offence, 16 counts of theft under $5,000, 15 counts of mischief over $5,000 and one count of theft over $5,000, police say. He was also taken into custody on two outstanding warrants tied to separate fraud investigations, according to police. Peel police say they are still looking for a 34-year-old woman believed to have been involved alongside him in the break-ins.

items.title: Mississauga Council Orders a Tariff-Relief Review and Eases a Park Fee for New Townhouses
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, council directed staff at its September 16 meeting to review potential tax relief measures, economic development initiatives and investment programs meant to support local businesses facing U.S. tariffs and broader trade uncertainty. The city says that review builds on Mississauga's existing trade response work, including support for export diversification, local supply chains and funding applications meant to help businesses reach new markets beyond the United States. Council also directed staff to examine how the city regulates businesses that sell tobacco, vapour and related nicotine products, looking at ways to strengthen municipal licensing, improve compliance monitoring and prevent youth access, the city says. Staff will work with Peel Public Health and other stakeholders on that review before reporting back with recommendations. Separately, council approved reducing the park enhancement contribution tied to a planned townhouse development at 2020 and 2040 Camilla Road from $450,000 to $225,000. According to the city, the reduction reflects updated city-wide amenity area requirements and the developer's commitment to move ahead with construction on schedule, and is meant to help facilitate the housing project while the development still provides more on-site amenity space than originally required.

items.title: Policorner Sets October 5 Date for a Mississauga Mayoral Debate Watched Well Beyond City Hall
items.summary: According to Policorner, a publication focused on Ontario provincial politics, the outlet will host a debate among Mississauga's leading mayoral candidates on Monday, October 5, at the Mississauga Civic Centre. Policorner says it decided to hold the 90-minute debate because the race has drawn unusually heavy provincial attention, given that it features two of only three people to have held the mayor's job since 1978. Premier Doug Ford weighed in on the race months before it began, telling reporters at a Mississauga construction site in March that he would send support to back Mayor Carolyn Parrish, according to Policorner. The outlet notes the contest pits Parrish, who has backing from Ford and his caucus, against her predecessor, a three-term mayor who left to lead the provincial Liberals and has spent much of the past three years opposing the Ford government. Two other candidates who finished second and third in the previous election are also competing for many of the same organizers and networks, Policorner reports.

items.title: 125 Volunteers Turn Out at Courtneypark Fields as Mississauga Works Toward a One Million Trees Goal
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, 125 volunteers planted 525 native trees and shrubs, including Sugar Maple, White Birch and White Spruce, at Courtneypark Athletic Fields on September 19 as part of TD Tree Days. The city selected Courtneypark Athletic Fields as part of a larger plan to naturalize roughly one hectare of mowed turf grass there. Officials say the new plantings will create habitat for wildlife, strengthen connections between nearby green spaces and, over time, provide added shade, carbon storage and improved air quality. The city has partnered with TD Tree Days since 2014 to bring volunteers together to restore natural areas and plant thousands of trees and shrubs across Mississauga, according to the city. These annual events support Mississauga's broader push to grow its urban forest and improve the health of local ecosystems, and specifically advance the city's One Million Trees program under its Natural Heritage and Urban Forest Strategy. The September 19 planting was the first of three TD Tree Days events planned at Courtneypark Athletic Fields, the city says.

items.title: Coroner's Jury Rules 2023 Death of Mississauga Senior an Accident, Calls for Crisis-Team Reforms
items.summary: A coroner's inquest jury has ruled the 2023 death of 88-year-old Mississauga resident John Brownlie an accident and issued 18 recommendations aimed at reforming how police and mental health crisis teams respond to similar calls. According to the inquest, Brownlie, a retired schoolteacher, died from complications of a blunt impact neck injury after falling down a flight of stairs during a struggle with a Peel Regional Police officer inside his Mississauga home. The inquest heard that Brownlie had been identified as a candidate for a visit from the Crisis Outreach and Support Team, known as COAST, on September 13, 2023, a day after his wife, Doris, called a crisis line seeking help. Among the jury's recommendations are mandatory body cameras for officers responding to mental health crisis calls and revised protocols for how those officers make first contact. The recommendations are intended to prevent similar deaths during future encounters between police and people in mental health crisis, according to the inquest jury's findings.
